exposure: Newly diagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism (ND-SCH) in early pregnancy
Previously known subclinical hypothyroidism (PK-SCH) before pregnancy
Previously known overt hypothyroidism (PK-OH) before pregnancy
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels in early pregnancy and near childbirth
outcome: LT4 retreatment in the first year postpartum
cohort: The study included 151 pregnant women, recruited from 1496 participants, who were classified into groups based on their hypothyroidism status (newly diagnosed subclinical, previously known subclinical, previously known overt) in early pregnancy.
finding: The prevalence of postpartum thyroiditis was comparable across women with newly diagnosed and previously known hypothyroidism, with specific TSH elevations at <8 gestational weeks, TSH levels outside 1.0-2.5 mU/L near childbirth, and TPOAb >=300 muIU/mL identified as risk factors for PPT and LT4 retreatment.
gest_age: 5-8 gestational weeks, first trimester (T1), <8 gestational weeks
